title: Linear Regression — Square the Misses
key_insight: Least squares adds the squared misses. Squaring makes every miss positive and makes large misses especially costly.
body:
## Square the Misses

A fitted line misses one price by 2 and another by 10. The larger miss should matter much more when choosing a better line.

Least squares adds the squared misses. Squaring makes every miss positive and makes large misses especially costly.

The fitted coefficients show how the prediction changes when one feature rises while the others stay fixed, but that is an association, not automatic proof of cause.
common_mistakes: Reading a learned weight as proof that one feature causes the answer.
Ignoring curved patterns left in the errors.
Comparing raw coefficient sizes when input units differ.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Square the Misses” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: It is a fast, explainable baseline for numeric prediction and a foundation for many later models.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Square the Misses” story, explain Linear Regression without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
